cases.note: No calls: nothing to dump and nothing to clean up.
openDB without a version creates version 1 and runs upgrade(0, 1).
A new database opened without an upgrade callback has no stores.
Version 1 then 2: upgrade(1, 2) adds a store, drops an index and writes in the upgrade transaction.
A lower version rejects with VersionError; 0, -1 and 2^53 throw TypeError synchronously.
Versions past 2^32 and up to 2^53 - 1, and a fraction, which IndexedDB truncates.
Failing schema calls inside upgrade are logged and the upgrade continues.
Aborting the first upgrade rejects the open with AbortError; a second open starts again at 0.
Aborting an upgrade of an existing database keeps version 1 and its data.
A failing add in the upgrade transaction aborts the upgrade and rejects the open.
A connection whose blocking callback closes it lets the upgrade proceed; it is then unusable.
blocking only logs, so blocked fires; its callback closes the old connection.
Without a blocking callback the old connection gets no call; blocked closes it.
deleteDB with an open connection: blocking(1, null), then blocked(1), then the delete resolves.
deleteDB with a connection that closes itself in blocking; the database is gone afterwards.
Closing and reopening without a version keeps the schema and data; no upgrade runs.
Two databases and a deleted third: only live databases are dumped.
Databases are dumped in the order they became live: one deleted and opened again moves to the end.
blocking closes the old connection at once, so the blocked callback is never called.
Each store method awaited in turn inside one readwrite transaction.
Index get, getKey, getAll, getAllKeys and count, with misses.
A miss resolves undefined, a stored null resolves null; null and range queries.
only, lowerBound, upperBound and bound with open ends; an empty bound throws DataError.
getAll counts: 0 means no limit; 2^32 and 2^32 + 1 throw TypeError (they do not wrap).
An absent argument is undefined, never null: null as a key, a direction or a mode throws; continue(null) moves on as continue() does.
A duplicate add: ConstraintError, AbortError for the rest and for done.
Requests queued then tx.abort(): every request and done reject with AbortError.
A put without a key path value throws DataError synchronously; the other requests still run.
Empty transactions: one completes, one aborts.
An uncaught DataError ends the script; the committed write is dumped and cleanup runs.
An uncaught ConstraintError ends the script; the transaction aborts.
A request issued while a caught error is still being dispatched is accepted, then aborted with the transaction.
A failure goes to the nearest enclosing step with catch: a transaction step absorbs it and skips the rest of its body.
Writing in a readonly transaction throws ReadOnlyError.
Unknown store, empty scope and an invalid mode throw; a caught failure keeps the script going.
tx.store is the only store, or undefined when the transaction has several.
tx.store on a finished transaction: undefined with several stores, InvalidStateError with one.
A batch on a finished transaction: the abort and every request throw InvalidStateError; done stays resolved.
After tx.done resolves, tx.store throws InvalidStateError (the transaction has finished); done stays resolved.
A nested readwrite transaction waits for the outer one; the outer done is awaited after it completed.
Two readonly transactions run together; the inner one reads while the outer is still active.
Explicit abort after an awaited put: done rejects, a second abort throws InvalidStateError.
An uncaught tx.done rejection ends the script after the abort.
Store cursor with continue, ascending and descending.
Index cursor: key, primary key and value; unique directions skip duplicates.
advance(2), advance(1.5) which IndexedDB truncates to 1, and advance past the end.
continue(key) jumps forward; a key behind the cursor throws DataError.
continuePrimaryKey on an index cursor; on a store cursor it throws InvalidAccessError.
cursor.update and cursor.delete in a readwrite walk.
openKeyCursor yields keys without values; update on a key cursor throws InvalidStateError.
cursor.update and delete in a readonly transaction throw ReadOnlyError.
A position without a move ends the walk; break ends it at once; a range with no match ends immediately.
Two moves at one position: the second throws InvalidStateError.
An invalid direction and a non-key continue throw TypeError and DataError.
A move that throws ends its position at once: the delete after it never runs, in a walk or in the iterator.
advance(0) throws TypeError; uncaught, it ends the script after the open.
A cursor over only(null) throws DataError before any request; uncaught, the script ends.
A 3000-record index walk with continue and a store walk with advance(7).
store.iterate with no moves continues automatically, in both directions.
Moves in the loop body are recorded and awaited by the iterator instead of continue().
cursor.update and cursor.delete inside the iterator body.
Breaking out of the iterator; the transaction is still usable.
Two moves in one body, a bad range and an index iterator over an empty match.
cursor.update after a move in the same body throws InvalidStateError; a break after a move ends the loop.
An iterator whose first move passes the end, and an index iterator that jumps with continue(key).
db.get, getKey, getAll, getAllKeys and count, and their FromIndex forms.
db.put, add, delete and clear wait for tx.done; the request error is reported first.
Close right after a shortcut write, then open version 2 with a blocked callback that is never called.
A shortcut whose key range throws rejects before any transaction; a failed write rejects with its own error.
A shortcut inside an open transaction runs after it; the outer transaction then finishes.
wrap(unwrap(source).method(...)) promisifies raw IndexedDB requests.
wrap with a second argument, and with a key range on an index.
Array key paths, array keys, a multiEntry index and a unique index violation.
String keys order by UTF-16 code units: an astral character sorts before U+E000.
Numeric keys past 2^31, 2^32 and 2^53, tiny and negative values; numbers sort before strings and arrays.
Key generators: out-of-line and in-line keys, an explicit key moves the generator.
A value nested 1000 levels deep and a 5000-element array round-trip.
Benchmark: 64 writes, 64 reads, index queries, an index walk with advance, an iterator and two shortcuts.
